purpose: Educational indicator dictionary for a fictional-mission prototype. Not a diagnostic system; defines no medical thresholds.

labels.[SIMULATION-ASSUMPTION]: Assumption introduced only for the fictional mission

indicators.definition: Heartbeats per minute in a point-in-time observation.
indicators.sampling: Compare only within the same measurement_context; the system baseline uses rest only. One resting reading per day at a similar time in the synthetic mission.
indicators.spaceflight_relevance: [EVIDENCE-SPACEFLIGHT] Night-time HR unchanged on the ISS (S4); HR unchanged while cardiac output increased (S5); the challenge mentions cardiovascular events (S1). Real monitoring with Bio-Monitor (S14).
indicators.limitations: Changes with exercise, sleep, stress, medication and posture; 60-100 is a general terrestrial reference, not a threshold for astronauts; do not infer arrhythmias or diagnoses.

indicators.definition: Peripheral oxygen saturation estimated by pulse oximetry.
indicators.sampling: Same position and context; compare within the person.
indicators.spaceflight_relevance: [EVIDENCE-SPACEFLIGHT] The 8.2 psia / 34% O2 exploration atmosphere introduces mild hypoxia (S8); in chamber tests there was no appreciable impact on SpO2 with mild exercise (S9).
indicators.terrestrial_reference: [TERRESTRIAL-CLINICAL] 96-100% at rest; may be lower at altitude or with some conditions (S16).
indicators.limitations: Sensor error, motion and perfusion; narrow range, small changes; not a diagnosis of hypoxia.

indicators.sampling: Count at rest for 1 minute (S15); do not mix with exercise or sleep.
indicators.spaceflight_relevance: [EVIDENCE-SPACEFLIGHT] The breathing pattern changes in microgravity (more abdominal contribution; lower tidal volume) (S6, S7); an increase of ~9% appears in a review without a confirmed primary source (S7).
indicators.limitations: Terrestrial references differ between sources; device estimation varies; small samples in spaceflight studies.

indicators.definition: Hours of sleep in the previous period, self-reported in the journal.
indicators.sampling: One entry per mission day; self-report.
indicators.spaceflight_relevance: [EVIDENCE-SPACEFLIGHT] Mean in-flight sleep ~6.0 h (5.96 shuttle; 6.09 ISS) with 8.5 h scheduled (S3); stress and tiredness increase in the second half of 6-month missions (S12, preliminary).
indicators.limitations: Self-report is less precise than actigraphy (S3 used both); does not measure sleep quality.

indicators.scale: integer 1-5: very low, low, neutral, high, very high
indicators.sampling: Once a day in the journal; no preselected value.
indicators.spaceflight_relevance: [EVIDENCE-SPACEFLIGHT] NASA BHP uses mood self-reports and the 37-item POMS as standard measures (S10); behavioral risk documented by HRP (S11).
indicators.limitations: [SIMULATION-ASSUMPTION] The product's 1-5 scale is NOT the POMS nor a validated clinical scale; ordinal: do not average.

indicators.definition: Self-reported perceived tiredness (optional, outside contract v0.1.0).
indicators.spaceflight_relevance: [EVIDENCE-SPACEFLIGHT] Tiredness appears in S12, and S3 mentions fatigue as a common complaint.
indicators.limitations: There is no contract field; it needs a team decision and a defined scale.

do_not_aggregate: Readings from different contexts (rest, exercise, sleep, unknown) in one baseline or trend.
Different astronauts, or synthetic with terrestrial data.
mood_score averages (ordinal), or mood presented as a clinical measure.
null converted to 0: a missing value is neither a normal nor an abnormal result.
Terrestrial ranges used as criteria for astronauts.
Sleep (daily journal) and vitals (point-in-time readings) in one series.
Environmental data (S21) treated as individual physiological measurements.

experimental_rules.summary: Resting heart-rate daily mean >= baseline + 5 beats/min on 2 consecutive days after the reference window.
experimental_rules.label: [SIMULATION-ASSUMPTION]
